title: Desk Guide — Approving RideLink Trip Mileage
content:
On the RideLink Mileage Reimbursement level of Non-Emergency Medical Transportation, the member's household drives the member to covered appointments and the company reimburses the miles. The desk books the reimbursement as an approved mileage entry on the member's reimbursement ledger.

## Rule

A trip's mileage entry is worked out from its registered outbound leg, which is the member's latest registered outbound leg, and it records the trip's reservation number, the round trip as its leg, the outbound leg's appointment date as its trip date and the approved miles. Mileage is reimbursed only on RideLink Mileage Reimbursement, for a trip registered with a trip number before the appointment.

For a trip whose return leg falls on a later date than its outbound leg and whose one-way miles reach the level's lodging threshold, the mileage entry is fixed only after the ledger carries the approved lodging and meals entry for that trip. Put the other way round: for such a trip, while the ledger does not yet carry that approved lodging and meals entry, the mileage entry is not fixed.

**Effect.** The approved mileage entry stands on the reimbursement ledger with a new member reimbursement claim number and is owed to the member until it is paid. The member sees the claim, its number, miles and amount in their reimbursement history.

## The booking tool

The entry is booked with `approve_trip_mileage_f67ba186`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`. One call books one approved mileage claim, dated today; nothing else on the benefit changes.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `ride_benefit_id` | Reference number of the member's transportation benefit, as the transportation benefit lookup returns it for the verified member | Identifier |
| `trip_number` | The trip's reservation number, as on the trip's registered legs or the member's confirmation | Verbatim, character for character (for example RL-5580213) |
| `leg` | Which part of the trip the claim covers | One of `outbound` (home to the appointment only), `return` (back home only), `round_trip` (the whole trip out and back), `not_applicable` (no trip leg) |
| `reimbursement_type` | The kind of reimbursement | One of `mileage` (the kind this booking records), `lodging_meals`, `late_pickup_alternative`, `not_applicable` (kinds this booking never records) |
| `claim_trip_date` | The trip date the claim is for | YYYY-MM-DD, a calendar date with no time or time zone |
| `approved_miles` | The approved miles | Miles to 1 decimal place (tenths of a mile), zero or more; stored rounded to 1 decimal |
| `amount` | The approved reimbursement amount | USD, 2 decimal places, positive; stored rounded to 2 decimals exactly as passed |

**Return.** A text dictionary: `status` is the literal "approved" when the claim was booked, which is the success receipt; `reimbursement_claim_number` is the new claim number in the form MR-YYMMDD-NNNN; `ledger_entry` is the reference of the new ledger entry; `trip_number`, `leg`, `reimbursement_type` and `claim_trip_date` echo what was booked; `approved_miles` is the miles booked with 1 decimal; `amount` is the approved USD amount with 2 decimals; `posted_date` is today's date as YYYY-MM-DD.
